chaines.hitbodedut_sihah: Say what is on your heart
chaines.hitbodedut_sihah_invite: Speak in your own language, as you would to someone. Everything on your heart, unrehearsed.
chaines.hitbodedut_harata_invite: Say what you regret, and say it plainly. Regret before Him is not putting yourself on trial.
chaines.hitbodedut_bakasha_invite: Ask for what you lack, and first of all to be brought close to Him. Even for what feels out of your reach.
chaines.hitbodedut_torah_invite: Take a teaching you heard today, and ask to reach it yourself.
chaines.hitbodedut_hodaa_invite: Give thanks for what you have been given, each as far as you are able. This is how you take leave.
chaines.onboarding_practice_body: Hitbodedut means withdrawing alone for a while each day and speaking to Hashem in your own language, as you would to someone. No formula to recite, no level to reach.
chaines.onboarding_private_body: The app only connects to the Internet when you ask it to: live flight tracking asks OpenSky Network for the aircraft in an approximate area, without sending the flight’s callsign; looking up a flight number sends only that number to adsbdb.com. What you write stays on this phone, and only you can take it out, through the export.

chaines.tips_hint: Ten pointers, to begin and to keep going.
chaines.tip_1_body: The first step in hitbodedut is to find a quiet place where you can be alone with yourself and with Hashem. It does not have to be entirely isolated, but it must be somewhere you will not be interrupted. A free room at home, a quiet stretch of beach, a spot out in nature. If you can, choose a natural setting: nature itself can be a source of inner quiet.
chaines.tip_2_body: If you are new to this, start short. Give fifteen minutes a day to hitbodedut, and lengthen it little by little, up to an hour if you can. Do not jump straight to a long hitbodedut. Go step by step, so that it becomes a habit and not a burden. Fix a regular time, so the practice becomes part of your day rather than something random.
chaines.tip_3_body: Begin the hitbodedut by speaking to Hashem, in your own words, in a whisper if need be. Do not worry if at first you do not know quite what to say. Simply open your heart and begin. It can be asking forgiveness, a plain prayer about what you feel, or a thank you. Hitbodedut does not have to be orderly or planned in advance. It is a place to set down what is in your heart and to turn towards Hashem.
chaines.tip_4_body: If you want to feel truly alone with yourself, avoid devices entirely during hitbodedut. Turn the phone off, or leave it in another room. The freer you are of outside distraction, the better you will connect to yourself and to Hashem. Cutting off from the outside world helps you concentrate and settle into the quiet within.
chaines.tip_5_title: Start with Tehillim, or your own words
chaines.tip_5_body: If you are not sure how to begin, open Tehillim and read a few chapters. The Psalms are prayer already formed, very direct, and they touch the soul. In hitbodedut they can be a spiritual thread leading you straight to Hashem. And if you feel you have no words, you can simply speak with Hashem freely, sharing your thoughts and what you feel.
chaines.tip_6_body: During hitbodedut, ask yourself inward questions. What am I feeling right now? What am I going through? How can I feel closer to Hashem? What do I need to improve in my life? This is a time for a real cheshbon nefesh. Sometimes, in the inner quiet, you come to see your real needs and the right direction for your life.
chaines.tip_7_body: During hitbodedut, do not try to hide from Hashem what you feel. This is a time when you are allowed to be honest with yourself and with Hashem. If you feel anger, frustration, fear or insecurity, this is the place to say it. Honesty is the key to spiritual growth. The more honest you are, the more inner quiet you will find.
chaines.tip_8_body: Hitbodedut can also be a time to make peace with yourself. That means being somewhere you are not judging, not criticizing, not angry at yourself. It is a time of reconciliation, where you forgive yourself, ask forgiveness for your mistakes, and resolve to mend your ways.
chaines.tip_9_body: Part of hitbodedut can be complete silence. When the words do not come, stay a while before Hashem without saying anything: being there, ready and wanting to speak, already counts (Likutei Moharan II, 25). In that silence, what is inside surfaces and comes clear.
chaines.tip_10_title: End with a deep breath and thanks
chaines.tip_10_body: At the end of hitbodedut, finish with a deep breath and bless Hashem for the time you spent together. It is a moment of thanks for the great gift of connection, and for the inner quiet you found. Even if you felt it was hard to find answers, do not worry: this meeting with yourself and with Hashem already brings spiritual abundance into your life.

chaines.levana_kippour_edot: Our custom: right after Yom Kippur (Yalkut Yosef 426:34)
chaines.levana_jeune: Tonight the fast ends: say it after tasting something (Mishnah Berurah 426:11)
chaines.levana_jeune_ashkenaz: Tonight the fast ends: the Rema waits for another night (426:2); the Acharonim say it after tasting something (Mishnah Berurah 426:11)

chaines.rappel_pluie_debut_edot: %1$s, in the Arvit Amida, we begin to say the winter blessing “בָּרֵךְ עָלֵינוּ”.
chaines.rappel_pluie_debut: %1$s, in the Arvit Amida, we begin to ask for rain: “וְתֵן טַל וּמָטָר לִבְרָכָה”.
chaines.rappel_pluie_fin_edot: From Pesach, we return to the summer blessing “בָּרְכֵנוּ”.
chaines.rappel_pluie_fin: From Pesach, we no longer ask for rain: “וְתֵן בְּרָכָה”.
chaines.rappel_guechem_debut: %1$s, at Musaf of Shemini Atzeret, we begin to say “מַשִּׁיב הָרוּחַ וּמוֹרִיד הַגֶּשֶׁם”.
chaines.rappel_guechem_fin: %1$s, at Musaf of the first day of Pesach, we stop saying “מַשִּׁיב הָרוּחַ וּמוֹרִיד הַגֶּשֶׁם”.
chaines.rappel_guechem_fin_ashkenaz: %1$s, at Musaf of the first day of Pesach, the chazan stops saying “מַשִּׁיב הָרוּחַ וּמוֹרִיד הַגֶּשֶׁם” in his repetition; the congregation still says it in the Musaf Amida and stops at Mincha (Rema and Mishnah Berurah 114:3).

chaines.vol_carte_sous: Enter a flight: times are computed along the planned route, on the device.
chaines.vol_methodes: Methods: dawn 16.1°, Misheyakir 11.5°, nightfall 8.5° below the horizon; Rabbeinu Tam 72 min; seasonal hours from sunrise to sunset (Gra) or from 72 min before to 72 min after (Magen Avraham). Calculated at sea level, on the device, offline.
chaines.vol_frise_retard: Calculated for the times entered. With a 30-min late departure, most of these times move by about %1$s min; the screen does not adjust by itself: edit the takeoff time.
chaines.vol_frise_retard_gps: Calculated for the times entered. With a 30-min late arrival, most of these times move by about %1$s min; the screen does not adjust by itself: edit the landing time, then take a new position reading.
chaines.vol_route_bouton: Find the arrival from the number
chaines.vol_route_trouvee: %1$s: %2$s. Departure %3$s, arrival %4$s. Route known to adsbdb.com, sometimes outdated: check it against your ticket.
chaines.vol_route_autre_depart: According to adsbdb.com, %1$s flies %2$s and does not depart from %3$s. Check the number or the departure airport; the known route may be outdated.
chaines.vol_route_inconnue: Airport %1$s, given by adsbdb.com, is not in the app’s list: choose it by hand.
chaines.vol_route_introuvable: adsbdb.com does not know this flight number: choose the airports by hand.
chaines.vol_route_invalide: Expected: the airline code then the number, for example LY81.
chaines.vol_route_erreur: Lookup failed (%1$s). You can still choose the airports by hand.
chaines.vol_source_adsbdb: Flight routes: adsbdb.com (data by David J. Taylor and Jim Mason)
chaines.vol_incomplet: Choose both airports and both times.
chaines.vol_invalide_meme_aeroport: Departure and arrival are the same airport.
chaines.vol_invalide_arrivee_avant_depart: Arrival must come after departure: check the dates, in each airport’s local time.
chaines.vol_invalide_trop_long: More than 22 hours of flight: check the arrival date.
chaines.vol_invalide_fuseau_inconnu: This device does not know this airport’s time zone.
chaines.vol_invraisemblable: The duration does not match the distance (%1$s km in %2$s): check the dates and AM/PM, in each airport’s local time. Tap “Calculate” again if the flight is correct.
chaines.vol_hors_fenetre: The calculation covers the flight and the 6 hours either side.
chaines.vol_ecart: %1$s min if departure is 30 min late
chaines.vol_fiabilite: Estimate along the planned route (great circle, constant speed between the times entered), not the aircraft’s real position. Zmanim of the point below the aircraft, at sea level, computed on the device, without network: seen from the aircraft, around 11,000 m, the sun rises earlier and sets later, by a quarter of an hour or more at mid-latitudes. Seasonal hours follow the day at that point, not the day as lived on board.
chaines.vol_reserve_haute_latitude: The route goes beyond 60° latitude: the degree-based and minute-based methods give very different times there, and some zmanim are missing.
chaines.vol_reserve_absent: Some zmanim do not occur on part of the route: beyond about 50° of latitude in summer, the sun does not go low enough for dawn (16.1°) or nightfall (8.5°); closer to the poles, midnight sun or polar night.
chaines.vol_reserve_absents: Missing on part of the route: %1$s.
chaines.vol_reserve_erreur: The calculation failed at a point on the route.
chaines.vol_reserve_a_rebours: The aircraft flies west faster than the sun: a zman occurs more than once.
chaines.vol_ligne_date: Date line (180th meridian) crossed around %1$s: the local date changes from %2$s to %3$s.
chaines.vol_jalons_titre: Shabbat, festivals and Omer during the flight
chaines.vol_jalons_note: Civil day of the point below the aircraft; %1$s, from the app setting.
chaines.vol_jalon_repli: No nightfall under the plane: fallback marker, a calculation choice (Omer and Arvit at sunset, end of Shabbat at Rabbenu Tam).
chaines.vol_omer_ligne_date: Date line during the Omer: your personal count (the nights you lived) and that of the place under the plane no longer match. According to Rav Shlomo Zalman Auerbach, one who lost a day continues without a blessing; according to the Lubavitcher Rebbe, one follows one’s personal count. Better avoid crossing the line during the Omer; ask your rav.
chaines.ligne_date_discutee: Date line: the app follows the international line (the local civil day). For Japan, New Zealand, eastern Australia, Hawaii, Tonga or Samoa, the poskim differ on the halachic line (Chazon Ish, Rav Tukachinsky, Rav Frank): ask your rav.
chaines.vol_gps_attente: Searching for a GPS signal… Reception is better near a window.
chaines.vol_gps_echec: No GPS position. The calculation stays on the planned route.
chaines.vol_gps_refuse: Without precise location, the calculation stays on the planned route.
chaines.vol_gps_hors_vol: The GPS fix is only used during the flight, between scheduled departure and arrival.
chaines.vol_fiabilite_gps: Route adjusted to the GPS fix of %1$s (%2$s), then great circle to arrival, at constant speed. Zmanim of the point below the aircraft, at sea level, computed on the device, without network.
chaines.vol_ecart_gps: %1$s min if arrival is 30 min late
chaines.vol_direct_explication: Off by default. When on, it sends the app’s relay the flight’s callsign and the aircraft’s estimated position, nothing else; the relay asks OpenSky Network for the real position. Over the oceans, the aircraft is often not seen.
chaines.vol_direct_activer: Online services: flight route and live tracking
chaines.vol_indicatif_invalide: Expected callsign: three letters then the number, for example ELY1.
chaines.vol_direct_introuvable: The aircraft is not seen right now (out of coverage or wrong callsign). The calculation stays on the planned route.
chaines.vol_direct_erreur: Tracking unavailable (%1$s). The calculation stays on the planned route.
chaines.vol_erreur_quota: today’s OpenSky quota is used up
chaines.vol_erreur_trop_de_demandes: too many requests: try again in a few minutes
chaines.vol_direct_inactif: The tracking relay is not in service yet in this version.
chaines.vol_direct_activer_web_aide: When on, the magnifier 🔍 sends only the flight number to adsbdb.com to fill in the arrival.
chaines.reglages_android_seulement: The morning gate (“I am with Hashem”) and the reminders exist only in the Android app.
chaines.vol_fiabilite_direct: Route adjusted to the position received from OpenSky Network at %1$s (%2$s), then great circle to arrival, at constant speed. Zmanim of the point below the aircraft, at sea level, computed on the device.
chaines.vol_rappels_aucun: No more reminders during this flight.
chaines.vol_rappels_sans_permission: The app’s notifications are off: the reminders will not show.
chaines.vol_rappels_note: At the ticket times: a late takeoff does not move the reminders. Android may delay them by a few minutes.
chaines.vol_rappel_derekh_texte: Scheduled takeoff was five minutes ago. Tefilat HaDerech, if you have not already said it for this journey.
chaines.vol_rappel_priere_texte: The time of %1$s begins below the aircraft. Until %2$s.
chaines.vol_rappel_priere_sans_limite: The time of %1$s begins below the aircraft.
chaines.vol_rappel_omer_texte: The stars come out below the aircraft: tonight is day %1$s of the Omer.
chaines.vol_rappel_gomel_texte_edot: Landed after a flight of 72 minutes or more: say HaGomel within three days, before ten men, preferably at the Torah reading (Yalkut Yosef 219:20).
chaines.vol_rappel_gomel_texte: Landed after a long flight: according to your custom, HaGomel is said within three days, before ten men (some require it after a flight, others do not).
chaines.vol_rappel_chema_mga: End of Shema (Magen Avraham): %1$s. If need be, per the Gra: %2$s.
chaines.vol_rappel_chema_gra: End of Shema (Gra): %1$s. Per the Magen Avraham: %2$s.
chaines.vol_direct_explication_opensky: Off by default. When on, it asks OpenSky Network, free and without an account, for the aircraft seen in a 10° square around the estimated position; the callsign stays on the phone, which looks for the flight there. Over the oceans, the aircraft is often not seen.

chaines.boussole_carte_sous: Choose a place: the figure turns toward Jerusalem.
chaines.boussole_legende: The ירושלים label (on the rose, the gold needle) follows the real direction; the dashed blue mark shows the direction on the map, for information.
chaines.boussole_a_plat: Hold the phone flat or upright in front of you, away from metal objects and magnets.
chaines.boussole_calibrer: Compass not accurate: draw a figure 8 in the air with the phone.
chaines.boussole_sans_capteur: This phone has no compass: the direction is given relative to north, at the top.
chaines.boussole_note: The direction of Jerusalem can be calculated in two ways. By the great circle, the real direction on the globe: the Shulchan Aruch HaRav (Orach Chaim 94:2), Rabbi Yaakov Emden’s Mor uKetziah (150) and others consider it preferable; from New York, about 54°. By the straight line on a Mercator map (constant heading), as read for example in the Levush (Orach Chaim 94): from New York, about 96°. The figure follows the one you choose under “Direction followed” (by default, the real direction); the other stays on screen for information. Calculated on the device, toward Har haBayit (31.7781° N, 35.2354° E), corrected for the local magnetic declination.
chaines.boussole_minyan: Here the two methods differ by more than 20°. In a minyan, pray in the direction of the congregation and turn only your face toward Jerusalem (Mishna Berura 94:10).
chaines.boussole_widget_description: The figure and the direction of Jerusalem from your zmanim location, relative to north. Tap to open the compass.
chaines.boussole_source_titre: Chabad.org, “Why Do We Face East When Praying? Or Do We?”
chaines.boussole_legende_carte: The ירושלים label (on the rose, the gold needle) follows the direction on the map; the dashed blue mark shows the real direction, for information.
chaines.divulgation_overlay_texte:
What is used: showing a screen over other apps.

Why: for the morning gate, the “I am with Hashem” mode, which you chose. When you open one of the apps you selected, during the time window you set, the “I am with Hashem” screen appears in front of it until the practice of the day is done. It also appears in front of these apps during any hitbodedut in progress, at any time of day, until it ends.

Nothing is sent or shared: everything stays on this phone.

To turn the gate off at any time: Settings, “I am with Hashem” switch. You can also remove this access in Android settings.
chaines.divulgation_usage_texte:
What is read: which app is shown in the foreground. Only the last one opened is kept, in memory; no history is stored.

Why: for the morning gate, the “I am with Hashem” mode, which you chose. During the time window you set, and until the practice of the day is done, the app checks whether the one just opened is among those you selected. It also checks during any hitbodedut in progress, at any time of day.

Nothing is recorded, sent or shared: everything stays on this phone.

To turn the gate off at any time: Settings, “I am with Hashem” switch. You can also remove this access in Android settings.
chaines.licences_texte:
Texts
The Hebrew texts (siddur, Tehillim, Tikkun, books, sources) come from public-domain editions, notably Sefaria, Torat Emet, tanach.us and rabenubook, or are used with their authors’ permission; each edition and its licence are declared in the app’s data files.
Yalkut Yosef – Kitzur Shulchan Aruch, by Rav Yitzchak Yosef: text from Torat Emet, CC BY-NC-SA 2.5 (creativecommons.org/licenses/by-nc-sa/2.5).
Hilulot: Hebrew Wikipedia (CC BY-SA 4.0), Torat Emet (CC BY-NC-SA 2.5), MyTzadik and HaMeir LaArets with their permission.

Translations
The French and English translations are machine-made and unreviewed: the Hebrew prevails. Those of Yalkut Yosef are partial, under the same licence as the text. For Tehillim, the Tikkun, Esther and Song of Songs: Bible du Rabbinat (1899) and JPS (1917), public domain.

Fonts
David Libre, Frank Ruhl Libre, Miriam Libre, Noto Rashi Hebrew, Noto Serif Hebrew and Varela Round, Secular One, Rubik, Heebo and Bellefair (app versions), under the SIL OFL 1.1 licence.

Data
Cities: GeoNames (CC BY 4.0). Airports: OurAirports (public domain); time zones: timezone-boundary-builder (ODbL, © OpenStreetMap contributors); names: Wikidata (CC0). Flight routes: adsbdb.com.

Calendar and zmanim
KosherJava (LGPL 2.1), directly or through its JavaScript port. The app ships with the licence text; the app’s source code is available on written request to myhitbodedut26@gmail.com.

chaines.vol_en_ligne_aide: Off by default: nothing leaves the phone. Once turned on, they stay on until you switch them off.
